title: Forward a local port to a remote service via SSH
summary: Create a secure tunnel that forwards traffic from a local port to a specific port on a remote server. This is often used to access services like web servers or databases securely.

steps.explain: Use the -L flag to forward a local port to a remote host and port. The -N and -T flags prevent opening a shell and disable pseudo-terminal allocation, keeping the connection purely for forwarding.

placeholders.name: USERNAME
placeholders.description: The username on the jump/ssh server

placeholders.name: REMOTE_HOST
placeholders.description: The hostname or IP of the ssh server

placeholders.name: LOCAL_PORT
placeholders.description: The port on your local machine to listen on

placeholders.name: REMOTE_TARGET
placeholders.description: The hostname or IP of the final target service

placeholders.name: REMOTE_PORT
placeholders.description: The port on the final target service
